The Following:
 Judgment

The appellants are before this Court being aggrieved by the dismissal of claim petition i.e. MVC No.576/2014 by the Fast Track Court II and Addl. MACT, Belagavi, (for short 'the tribunal') filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

2. Heard Sri. Vitthal S.Teli, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri. Shivakumar S. Badawadagi,
learned counsel for the respondent-corporation.
Perused the appeal memo as well the tribunal records.

3. The facts of the case are that, the appellants are wife, children and father of the deceased Shivarudra Langote, who died in a road traffic accident involving KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-25/F2736 and Maruti car bearing registration No.KA-25/N5516.

On 16.07.2023, when the Suman W/O Shivarudra Langote vs The Divisional Controller on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99774181/
2 deceased was proceeding from Dharwad to Hubballi in his car, the accident took place between KSRTC bus and the car which is driven by the deceased.

entities.text: Suman W/O Shivarudra Langote vs The Divisional Controller
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Due to the injuries sustained by the deceased, he died on the spot.
The Conductor of the KSRTC bus lodged complaint to the police with regard to the accident.

4. Later, the claimants i.e. the legal heirs of the deceased Shivarudra Langote filed claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V.Act, 1988, seeking compensation for the death of the deceased Shivarudra Langote, who was working as a Lecturer and was receiving a consolidated salary of Rs.31,000/- per month.

5. The respondent-NWKRTC appeared and filed its objections and denied the averments of the claim petition and in its objections, it was specifically stated that, the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Maruti car.
It is also stated that, the deceased lost control over the vehicle and went to the wrong side of the road and dashed to the on coming NWKRTC bus.

6. The wife of the deceased examined herself as P.W.1 and one Kallangouda A Patil, was examined as P.W.2 and Jagadish M. Shetter, was examined as P.W.3, apart from examining three witnesses,
claimants marked documents from Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.

The respondent- NWKRTC examined one Mr.
Kuberappa B. Harti as R.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R.3.

7. On appreciation of the materials on record the tribunal by its Judgment and award dated 16.09.2014 dismissed the claim petition of the claimants on the ground that, the accident took place solely due to the negligent driving of the driver of the car i.e. deceased Shivarudra Langote.

8. Learned counsel Sri. Vitthal S. Teli, would submit that, only on the ground that the complaint is filed by the conductor of the bus and the charge-sheet is filed against the deceased, the tribunal could not have come to the conclusion that, the accident took place solely due to the negligence of the deceased.

Learned counsel would submit that, the sketch and photographs even though shows that the car had moved to the wrong side and dashed to the bus, placing reliance only on the sketch is wholly erroneous.
9. Learned counsel would further submit that, P.W.2 is an eyewitness and the tribunal has failed to appreciate the evidence of P.W.2.

Learned counsel would place reliance on the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others,
reported in (2015) 5 SCC 656 to contend that the tribunal could not have placed reliance on the sketch and based on the record ought to have come to the conclusion that, it is a case of contributory negligence, but the tribunal erroneously dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the deceased was solely responsible for occurrence of the accident.
10.

Learned counsel would also refer to the evidence of P.W.2 eyewitness and submits that, P.W.2 had admitted that, he saw the car only on getting down from the bus in which he was traveling.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

11. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material on record, the only point that would arise for our consideration is "Whether, the Judgment and award under appeal requires interference?"
12.

Our answer to the above point would be in the negative for the following reason:
There is no dispute with regard to the accident that had taken place on 16.07.2013 between NWKTC bus bearing No.KA-25/N5516 and Maruti car bearing registration No.KA-25/N-5516 and the death of the deceased Shivarudra Langote, the husband of the appellant No.1/claimant No.1.
The deceased Shivarudra Langote was driving his Maruti car from Dharwad to Hubballi and dashed to the NWKRTC bus which was coming from the opposite direction.
It is an admitted fact that the complaint was filed by the Conductor of the bus with regard to the accident between NWKRTC bus and the car and no complaint is filed from the claimants' side.
It is also an admitted fact that, the charge-sheet is filed against the deceased i.e. the driver of the car.
A perusal of the sketch would indicate that, though it was a double road, one of its way was blocked as there was some repair works to the road.

The NWKRTC bus was moving on the left side of the road and the car which was coming from the opposite direction,
was driven to the right side and dashed to the NWKRTC bus.
The photographs which are placed on record as Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 would clearly indicate that the car was completely driven to the right side of the road and dashed to the on coming NWKRTC bus.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that, P.W.2 is an eyewitness and his evidence has not been appreciated properly.
We have gone through the evidence of P.W.2.
P.W.2 has stated that, at the time of accident he was traveling in the bus and stated that, the bus was moving on the left side of the road.
Further, he says that, for the first time he saw the car after the accident and after getting down from the bus.
When he was confronted with the photographs i.e. Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 the witness P.W.2 admits the contents of the same and says that it is true and correct.

When P.W.2 states in his evidence that he saw the car for the first time after getting down from the bus, he cannot be considered as an eyewitness, since he has not seen the accident and only saw the car after getting down from the bus.
Learned counsel for the appellants has placed reliance on the Mangla Ram case and contended that, the tribunal ought not to have placed reliance on the sketch.
The facts of the said case is entirely different from the present case.

In the said case, the motorcycle involved in the accident was pushed forward after collusion and after Suman W/O Shivarudra Langote vs The Divisional Controller on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99774181/
4 being hit by the offending vehicle.
13.
